title: Чужая чашка у бара  (Someone Else's Mug at the Bar)

segments.t: While Senya and Fedya continue their loud feud over Maxim Galkin in the kitchen, a new conflict breaks out at the bar counter. Exhausted after a restless night, Sasha casually drinks coffee out of Nastya's personal mug, leaving Kostya caught in the middle.
Не могу проснуться, всю ночь плохо спала.
В смысле у меня и у тебя.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'Come on, say that one more time.' Coming on say that one more time is how Barinov lays out the situation for Kostya.

'Do you even know who your Galkin is?' Here checking whether Barinov even know who Barinov's Galkin is shows Kostya looking for the real truth. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
'Who? Got it?' With the plan and moment hanging in the air, Lyova puts Barinov on the spot.
'Kostya, please pass me my coffee.' Telling Kostya to pass him his coffee moves the conversation forward without extra drama.
Не могу проснуться, всю ночь плохо спала.
'I cannot wake up, I slept terribly all night.' Kostya explains that he cannot wake up he slept terribly all night, keeping his voice calm and direct.
'Thank you very much.' Between the truth and the kitchen, Lyova gives Barinov a quick, grounded response.
В смысле у меня и у тебя.

'What do you mean, mine and yours.' Barinov explains that what do Kostya means, keeping his voice calm and direct. Russian expresses having something as "by me is", keeping the phrase short and grounded.

'What do you mean, I took it?' Asking what Barinov means he took it cuts straight through the tension between Kostya and Barinov. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'We will figure something out.' Noting that they will figure something out keeps Lyova's side of the story simple and clear.
'There is Galkin for you.' Even though there is Galkin for Kostya, Barinov keeps a steady face in front of Kostya.
'While in Russia everything is the other way around.' Admitting that while in Russia everything is the other way around shows Kostya being honest for a change.
'What? Really?' With the morning and coffee hanging in the air, Lyova puts Barinov on the spot.

'And what about this!' Over the morning and the moment, Barinov lets his real feelings show. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Не могу проснуться, всю ночь плохо спала.
В смысле у меня и у тебя.

That wraps up this scene as while Senya and Fedya keep bickering over Galkin in the kitchen, Sasha irritates Nastya at the bar by drinking morning coffee out of Nastya's favorite mug. Until next time!
